content:
I upgraded to the Apple Watch Series 12 last week, and after a few days of testing, three features left a particularly deep impression on me.

#1: S11 chip makes everything smoother

Apple Watch's chip update has been a long time coming — Apple skipped a generation entirely last year, with no real performance boost since the S9.

I'm happy to report that the new S11 chip is noticeably faster and more powerful than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday operations on the Apple Watch Series 12 feel very smooth. Among them, watchOS 27's headline feature, Siri AI, seems tailor-made for this latest hardware. When I tested it on older hardware, Siri had always felt rather sluggish, but running on the Series 12, it finally comes close to the experience I had in mind.

#2: Brand-new health features and complications

The new Health Sensing System should make the Apple Watch Series 12 more accurate at tracking key metrics such as heart rate and step count. However, this time the improvements go well beyond just accuracy.

Thanks to the new health sensors, the Series 12 offers three complications that weren't available before:

  • Heart rate
  • Daily steps
  • Readiness

You can view the latest heart rate, step count and readiness score right on the watch face.

I've already tried the heart-rate complications, but Readiness needs more data before it can be used. Overall, these new features are extremely practical and bring a meaningful boost to the Apple Watch's health and wellness capabilities.

#3: Faster charging

Overall battery life on the Apple Watch Series 12 is roughly on par with the Series 11, though you can squeeze 25% more usage out of it during outdoor workouts.

Longer battery life is certainly welcome, but what I like even more about the Series 12 is the faster charging speed. Here's how it compares with the Series 11:

  • Apple Watch Series 12: 15 minutes of charging delivers up to 12 hours of use
  • Apple Watch Series 11: 15 minutes of charging delivers up to 8 hours of use

I'm used to sleeping with my Apple Watch on, and after work I usually want to top it back up as quickly as possible, but sometimes I simply don't have time to wait for it to charge. Fortunately, the Series 12 supports faster charging, so even when my schedule isn't ideal, it's not a problem.

If you'd like to read more hands-on thoughts about the Series 12, check out my colleague Chance's full review.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is now officially on sale, starting at US$399.

Have you upgraded to the Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Feel free to share in the comments.
